media:group.media:title: Inaugural of Tom Ellis
media:group.media:description: In his inaugural lecture, Professor Tom Ellis explores how synthetic biology is allowing researchers to rewrite DNA and programme microbes to grow sustainable materials. Living Code, Living Materials looks at the emerging field of Engineered Living Materials, including the use of engineered cells to create sustainable fabrics, functional bio-composites and self-repairing materials. Professor Ellis also considers how programming nature could support more sustainable approaches to manufacturing, food production and infrastructure. Professor Tom Ellis is Professor of Synthetic Genome Engineering in the Department of Bioengineering at Imperial College London. His research focuses on synthetic biology, genome engineering, and developing biological systems to address challenges in health, sustainability, and manufacturing. Recorded at Imperial College London on 4 November 2026 as part of Imperial’s Inaugural Lecture series.

entry.title: Cracking the code: targeting HTLV integration to eradicate infection

media:group.media:title: Cracking the code: targeting HTLV integration to eradicate infection
media:group.media:description:
HTLV affects an estimated 10 million people worldwide, yet remains one of the world’s most neglected viruses. Once it infects a cell, the virus becomes part of its DNA, allowing the infection to persist for life.
Join Professor Goedele Maertens, Professor of Retrovirology, to explore how HTLV establishes infection and how existing HIV drugs could offer a promising way to prevent transmission. #ImperialInaugurals
For more information about events at Imperial College London visit our website: https://www.imperial.ac.uk/whats-on/

entry.title: How to improve tuberculosis and chronic lung disease care in Africa | Research at Imperial

media:group.media:title: How to improve tuberculosis and chronic lung disease care in Africa | Research at Imperial
media:group.media:description:
How can health systems better support people living with tuberculosis (TB) and chronic lung disease? In this video, Dr Jamilah Meghji from Imperial College London discusses her international collaborative research into integrating TB and respiratory care across urban settings in Africa, with the aim of improving patient outcomes and making care more effective for health systems.
Imperial’s National Heart and Lung Institute is home to leading expertise in respiratory research. Study with us to learn from global experts and be part of research with real-world impact: https://www.imperial.ac.uk/nhli/study/

entry.title: The Frontiers in Natural Sciences: The Dean’s Annual Lecture 2026

media:group.media:title: The Frontiers in Natural Sciences: The Dean’s Annual Lecture 2026
media:group.media:description:
The Frontiers in Natural Sciences: The Dean’s Annual Lecture 2026, delivered by Geordie Williamson on the subject of ‘AI and the long conversation of mathematics’.
The lecture was followed by a panel discussion on the current state of AI within Mathematics. Professor Williamson will be joined on the panel by Ulrike Tillmann, Professor of Mathematics at the University of Oxford, Director of the Isaac Newton Institute at the University of Cambridge, and former President of LMS; Ana Caraiani, Royal Society University Research Fellow; and Kevin Buzzard, Professor of Pure Mathematics at Imperial College London.

media:group.media:title: IN-CYPHER Conference
media:group.media:description:
Cyber-security, healthcare, medical devices, data, patient safety, and finding solutions in emerging technologies.
On 23 to 24 September, we brought together leading researchers, healthcare professionals, and industry experts to explore the evolving frontiers of hardware security and cybersecurity. The conversations at IN-CYPHER conference 2026 were insightful, the ideas were inspiring and the collaboration was global.
IN-CYPHER is a joint research programme between Imperial College London and Nanyang Technological University Singapore funded by National Research Foundation Singapore.
